title: WHO: about 1.16 million people a year die in road traffic crashes
summary: WHO's road-injury sheet says those crashes are the leading cause of death for people aged 5 to 29, and that 20 to 50 million more people are injured.
body: WHO's road-traffic-injuries fact sheet, dated 20 July 2026, says approximately 1.16 million people die each year as a result of road traffic crashes. It says road traffic injuries are the leading cause of death for children and young adults aged 5 to 29 years. It says more than half of all road traffic deaths are among pedestrians, cyclists, and motorcyclists, and that between 20 and 50 million more people suffer non-fatal injuries. It says 92 percent of the world's road fatalities occur in low- and middle-income countries, which have around 60 percent of the world's vehicles. The 1.16 million is the sheet's annual figure.
